newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: U.N.'s Annan appeals for aid for new Zaire govt.
newsitem.headline: U.N.'s Annan appeals for aid for new Zaire govt.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Monday the United Nations was ready to work with a new government in Zaire and appealed to the international community to help the country to recovery.
"Ours is a big tent, we work with all governments and we will work with the new government," Annan, who is on a three-day visit to Vienna, told reporters.

Japan, a major importer of metals from Zaire, has hinted it would recognise the government of rebel leader Laurent Kabila, following a similar move by South Africa and cautious endorsement by the United States.
Annan said he had appealed for several months for a peaceful transition of power.
"I am gratified there was no major bloodshed in Kinshasa," he added.

Local Red Cross officials put the death toll over two days at about 200, many of them looters shot by rebel troops trying to keep order but also former soldiers loyal to dictator Mobutu Sese Seko killed by lynch mobs.
Annan said he had spoken to the U.N. special envoy in Zaire Mohamed Sahnoun, and that he had conveyed a message through Sahnoun to Kabila in talks on Sunday.

The U.N. chief said he now hoped Kabila would set to work on forming a broad-based government to include other political opposition movements apart from his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL).
"We should not forget that apart from the alliance there have been other political opposition movements in Zaire and the other political movements wil have to be brought in," he said.
"In time the government under Kabila will organise elections and I hope the international community will assist," he added.
Annan said Zaire not only needed help from outside with establishing its new institutions, but the huge central African state and the whole region needed aid for reconstruction.

"I appeal to the international community to work for the recovery of Zaire and I think if we handle it properly and work with the government...we can set Zaire on the road to national reconciliation, democracy and eventual prosperity..," Annan said.
